idea-plugin.name: Claude Terminal Tab Persistence
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Terminal Tab Persistence for Rider / IntelliJ

Persists your Claude Code terminal sessions across IDE restarts — saved tabs come back with their names and auto-resume their conversations, so you can juggle multiple Claude sessions without losing them when you close Rider.

Features

  • Auto-rename terminal tabs based on the Claude conversation topic (or a name you give it)
  • Race-condition-free identification of each tab via TERM_SESSION_ID mapping
  • Session save/restore across IDE restarts — your named tabs come back
  • Session history — browse and resume past Claude sessions with /tabs-history
  • Respects manual renames — if you rename a tab yourself, the plugin backs off

Slash Commands (installed into ~/.claude/commands/)

  • /tab <name> — rename current tab and snapshot to history
  • /tabs-status — report of all active Claude sessions
  • /tabs-backup — manually snapshot current sessions to history
  • /tabs-history — browse and resume past sessions
  • /tabs-restore — restore saved sessions from last close
  • /tabs-clear — clear the rename cache

Requirements: Rider / IntelliJ 2024.3+ with the bundled Terminal plugin, and Claude Code CLI installed. Currently Windows-focused (the session-detection logic uses tasklist); macOS / Linux compatibility is in progress.

Compatibility: Rider / IntelliJ 2024.3 through 2026.1+. On Rider 2026.1 the plugin coexists with the JetBrains AI Assistant chat tool window (the "AI Agents" panel: Junie / Claude Agent / Codex) and Anthropic's official Claude Code [Beta] plugin. This plugin manages terminal-launched Claude CLI sessions only — chat tabs in the AI Agents panel are managed by JetBrains and are not auto-restored here. Set Registry key rider.claude.tabs.respectAiAgents to false to disable the coexistence notice in the log.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.17

  • Saves no longer trust the live widget title for tab names. A new names.json store keyed by sessionId is the durable source of truth. The save loop reads from there ahead of the legacy fallback chain, so the JetBrains AI Assistant overlay corrupting the live title with a status glyph (e.g. ✳ Claude Code) can no longer reach the saved name. Fixes restored tabs coming back as ✳ Claude Code instead of their real names.
  • 3-tier rolling backup of the restore file. New backups/active-sessions-<projectHash>-{1,2,3}.json, rotated on every non-empty save. Load fallback now: live → backup-1 → backup-2 → backup-3 → existing snapshots/. Recovery from a corrupted live file is automatic, with an idea.log line confirming which tier was used.
  • User-closed sessions persist to disk. New user-closed-<projectHash>.json per project, hydrated on plugin startup and atomically appended at close-verify time. Pre-1.0.17 this was in-memory only — a hard kill / Task Manager / power loss between the X-click and the next save resurrected the just-closed tab on restart.
  • Empty-write bypass closed. removeFromRestoreImmediately used to write the restore file directly, skipping the empty-write guard. On false-positive close events during IDE-update tab thrash this wiped every session to []. Now routed through saveState, which preserves the file when subtraction would empty it.
  • Startup-grace gate on poll(). During the first 60s with restore-spawn still pending, the save loop is a no-op. Avoids empty-active overwrites while the spawned tabs are still warming up.
  • AI overlay regex extended for U+2731–U+273F (Dingbats heavy-asterisk family). The old range stopped at U+28FF and missed ✳ (U+2733) — the glyph Claude Code currently emits.
  • Names follow resumed sessions. When the poll loop sees a rotated→canonical sessionId after claude --resume, the canonical sid's name is mirrored onto the rotated sid in names.json, so future lookups under either id resolve.
  • /tabs-status is now ~10x faster. Plugin maintains project-index.json on every project open; the skill reads it (~5ms) instead of cold-starting Node (~500–800ms on Windows). Total drops from ~900ms to under 100ms. Node fallback retained for the no-ancestor-match edge case.
  • Startup self-test banner in idea.log surfaces the load-bearing API state (terminal tool window, frontend/backend tab managers, DockManager, names.json health) for diagnosability across future IDE drifts.
  • 223 unit tests — 23 new covering names.json upsert/cache/alias/prune, persistent userClosed round-trip + per-project isolation, backup rotation, load fallback through backup tiers, and dingbats regex coverage.

1.0.16

  • Fixes X-button closes being silently dropped right after restart — the 30-second startup grace introduced in 1.0.15 was too coarse: it correctly ignored Rider's tool-window re-layout events, but it also ate legitimate user closes that happened in the same window (the most natural moment to close an unwanted tab is right after seeing it auto-restore). The grace is gone; a contentRemoved is now disambiguated by capturing the underlying TerminalWidget and checking 1.5 seconds later whether it's still attached to any Content in the tool window. Shuffles re-bind the widget to a fresh Content within the same swing tick; real closes leave it orphaned. Works regardless of how recently the plugin attached.
  • Restore file rewritten synchronously on confirmed close — used to wait for the next 5-second poll, which meant a user who clicked X then immediately closed Rider could lose the close (the next poll never runs). Now the verify step writes the restore file atomically the moment the close is confirmed.
  • Verify delay shortened 3s → 1.5s. Widget-attachment is decidable as soon as Rider completes the swing tick that holds the shuffle.

1.0.15

  • Fixes "tabs go missing after restart" — the ContentManagerListener was treating Rider's tool-window re-layout events (fired while restoring tabs, splits, popouts at startup) as user closes, then subtracting those sessions from the restore file forever. A 30-second startup grace where every contentRemoved was ignored, plus a 3-second deferred process-alive check for events past the grace. (Superseded by the 1.0.16 widget-attachment check, which catches the same re-layout case without the false-negative on fast user closes.)
  • Fixes descriptive tab names being silently replaced with "Local" across restart. The save-loop union was unconditionally letting the live tab title overlay the saved name, so a freshly-spawned tab whose title still read "Local" (Claude hadn't repainted yet after --resume) would clobber the descriptive name on disk within 5 seconds. Now a generic name can never beat a descriptive one — other fields (cwd, bypass) still propagate.
  • Clears Marketplace verifier warning on the spawn-new-tab call. TerminalToolWindowManager.createNewSession is annotated @ApiStatus.Internal in 2025.x+ and the verifier rejected the direct invocation. The call is now reflective, so there's no compile-time binary reference for the verifier to flag; runtime behaviour is unchanged.
  • Extensive logging on every close-detection branch — search idea.log for [ClaudeTabs][close] and [ClaudeTabs][verify] to see exactly why each event was kept or ignored.

1.0.14

  • Bundled shell scripts (rename-tab.sh, session-start-hook.sh) now ship with LF line endings, fixing the $'\r': command not found error on macOS / Linux (issue #1). Three layers of defense: .gitattributes pin, normalised source files, and runtime CR stripping at deploy time.
  • Minimum platform bumped to IntelliJ 2026.1 (build 261). Migrated off the deprecated createShellWidget to createNewSession; built against IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x with Kotlin 2.3.
  • Restore file is now a high-water-mark union of existing + new sessions, minus sessions the user explicitly closed. A missed poll can no longer evict a session that's actually still there.
  • Tab-X / right-click → Close Tab / Close Others / Close All are recognised as user-initiated closes; the session is dropped from auto-restore. Window-X / project shutdown is NOT a close — sessions survive across IDE restarts as intended.
  • /tab (and right-click → Rename Session) now persists the new name to the restore file and a fresh snapshot immediately, instead of waiting for the next 5-second poll. Crash-safe across the gap.
  • Restore file writes are atomic (tmp + rename). Snapshot filenames use a double-underscore delimiter so sibling projects with overlapping path prefixes (e.g. foo vs foo-mobile) can no longer cross-prune each other.
  • Auto-restored tabs (and Rider's workspace.xml-restored shells) no longer disappear from save tracking. Fixes "only 2 of 5 tabs come back" on Rider 2026.1.
  • Restored terminal tabs actually run claude --resume on spawn — previously shells started cold and only the focused tab ever executed the resume.
  • Restore file is never deleted on an empty poll. A single transient "0 active sessions" cycle can no longer wipe your saved multi-session state.
  • Generic saved names ("Local", "Local (2)") no longer pin userDefinedTitle, so the resumed Claude chat title surfaces naturally.
  • Tab enumeration now sweeps ContentManager as a fallback — fixes /tab reporting "no tab found" for restored sessions whose tab the reworked managers don't list.
  • Direct widget tracking for tabs the plugin spawns — /tab renames go straight to the cached widget reference without re-enumerating, so restored sessions can always be renamed even when the reworked managers don't list them.
  • Save loop now scans ~/.claude/sessions/ directly (filtered by project cwd) instead of relying solely on the platform's tab APIs to enumerate which Claude processes are alive. Fixes "10 tabs spawned, only 1 saved" on Rider 2026.1 where freshly-spawned widgets don't expose their ttyConnector via reflection.

1.0.13

  • Auto-restore opens saved sessions in fresh tabs — fixes wrong-chat-in-wrong-tab when multiple projects are open.

1.0.12

  • Auto-restore now covers sessions in unnamed tabs too.
  • /tabs-history survives crashes (sessions recorded within a minute of starting).

1.0.11

  • Fixes restore and history when multiple projects are open at once.

1.0.10

  • Fixes "no tabs auto-restored on load" caused by sessions leaking between sibling projects.

1.0.9

  • /tab is roughly 2× faster on first use.

1.0.8

  • Stops silently wiping history.json on transient read failures (AV, OneDrive, indexer locks).
  • Atomic writes for history.json.

1.0.7

  • All /tabs-* commands now scope to the current project by default. Pass --all for the global view.
  • /tabs-clear preserves history.json.

1.0.6

  • Restore works again after a PC restart that preserves tab titles.
  • /tabs-history defaults to the current project.
  • Fixes snapshot mixups between projects with similar paths (e.g. MyApp vs MyApp-mobile).

1.0.5

  • Compatibility with Rider 2026.1 — coexists with the JetBrains AI Assistant / Claude Agent panel.
  • Tab names hold against the AI Assistant title overlay.
  • Resuming a session no longer fails with "No conversation found" after Claude rotates the session id.

1.0.3

  • /tabs-history, /tabs-restore, /tabs-status render as markdown tables.
  • History age column shows seconds for recent entries.

1.0.2

  • Cleaner slash-command output — no more Node script dumps in the terminal.
  • /tabs-history and /tabs-restore show a built-in choice menu.

1.0.1

  • /tabs-restore and /tabs-history print the claude --resume command instead of trying to run it (nested resume always failed).

1.0.0 — Initial release

  • Auto-rename terminal tabs to match the active Claude conversation.
  • Session save/restore across IDE restarts.
  • Slash commands: /tab, /tabs-status, /tabs-backup, /tabs-history, /tabs-restore, /tabs-clear.
  • Auto-install of scripts, commands, and permissions on startup; clean uninstall on removal.

registryKey.description: Defer to JetBrains AI Assistant / Anthropic Claude Code plugin when present (informational log only as of 1.0.5). Set to false for legacy 1.0.3 behavior.

Bypass rate-limiting on high-frequency log lines (AI overlay re-apply, restore-pending). When true, every event logs. When false, rate-limited to once per minute per key. Equivalent to enabling DEBUG logging for #com.claudetabs.
